newsitem.title: USA: U.S. judge favors rock band over Pinkerton.
newsitem.headline: U.S. judge favors rock band over Pinkerton.

text.p: A judge in Los Angeles has overturned a court order obtained by the Pinkerton detective agency that prevented popular rock band Weezer from selling its new album, the two sides said on Thursday.
Pinkerton was upset that Weezer called the album "Pinkerton", although a band spokesman said the title referred to the villainous lead character in Puccini's "Madame Butterfly" opera.

U.S. District Court Judge John G. Davies "dissolved" the temporary restraining order he originally issued Monday, saying the immediate financial hardship would be greater on Weezer and its Geffen Records label, said Pinkerton spokesman Dereck Andrade.
"We're not surprised at all," Andrade said in an interview, noting that his company still had a $2 million trademark infringement suit outstanding against Geffen and Weezer in federal court.
He hoped there could be "suitable resolution" such as Geffen paying Pinkerton a licensing fee, plastering albums with a disclaimer sticker, or changing the name of the album.

He said the issue was "not a laughing matter", as Pinkerton goes to great lengths to protect its federally registered trademark. The Encino, Calif,-based security firm was founded in 1850 by original "private eye" Allan Pinkerton, and is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
